newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bullish German shares surge to record highs.
newsitem.headline: Bullish German shares surge to record highs.

text.p: German shares surged to new record highs in bourse and electronic trade on Monday, driven by a wave of bullish sentiment after last Friday's jump in the dollar and Wall Street stocks.
The DAX index of Germany's leading 30 blue chip shares cruised past the 2,600 threshold for the first time to end the session up 33.91 points, or 1.3 percent, at 2,629.87.
Germany's IBIS index of all-day electronic trade pushed higher after the bourse close, ending slightly higher at 2,630.24 after earlier setting a record-high of 2,632.51.
The bourse advance, partly a delayed reaction to a U.S. rally later on Friday, was viewed in the market as confirming that the DAX is set to shoot ahead after months in seasonal doldrums.
"One minute it's the summer lull and now it's Christmas," said one Frankfurt dealer, who said there had been healthy interest from foreign institutional buyers.
"It looks as if the (German) market wants to keep going higher and few believe the gains will stop for now," said another dealer.
Long-term projections pinned the DAX's next stop as high as 2,750, well in line with the most optimistic forecasts from the start of the year, rarely mentioned in recent weeks.

Short-covering of "sell" positions on September DAX futures contracts, which expire later this week, was also seen as helping the market higher. September DAX futures were 16 points higher at 2,631 in early afternoon.

Among specific shares, chemical concern Bayer AG rose 1.16 marks to 56.03 after a newspaper report later confirmed, that it was launching a U.S. joint venture with Roche Holding Ltd in the U.S to sell Roche's Aleve analgesic and other products.

Print equipment manufacturer Linotype Hell also got a boost to end up five marks at 100 marks after holders of 25 percent of its shares accepted a buy offer which will allow its rival Heidelberger Druck to take the group over.
